title: A quasi-regular sequence followed by a sequence that is H1-regular modulo the ideal it generates is quasi-regular
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The lemma is the gluing statement for quasi-regularity, the analogue of the H1-regular gluing proved in the same section: if I is generated by a quasi-regular sequence f_1 to f_n and the images of g_1 to g_m are H_1-regular in A/I, then the juxtaposition is quasi-regular in A (statement lines 7522-7528). Its 43-line proof (proof lines 7531-7573) first establishes by induction on d that g_1 to g_m stay H_1-regular modulo every power I^d, using a short exact sequence of Koszul complexes and the fact that a quasi-regular sequence makes I^{d-1}/I^d a direct sum of copies of A/I; then it takes an element of J^{d+1} with J generated by all f and g, decomposes it by multinomial degree, applies the quasi-regularity of the g's modulo I^{d-e+1}, then the preceding intersection lemma of the same section, and finally the quasi-regularity of the f's to reach the required membership a_{N,M} in J. Both halves are genuine inductions and the second one needs the intermediate lemma to convert an intersection statement into a membership statement.
